scenarios.title: Set up named local accounts and their access levels
scenarios.summary: Configure explicit local identity checks, retain two different access levels and diagnose failed training logins.
scenarios.objective: Keep only LeadAdmin and Observer as local accounts, using an explicit case-sensitive local login method and local EXEC authorization. LeadAdmin must authenticate with training word Lab-Lead-42 and receive privileged EXEC level 15; Observer must authenticate with Lab-Observe-93 and receive user EXEC level 1. Reject wrong training words, unknown accounts, and the supplied differently cased account name. Preserve every supplied incoming SSH version 2, Telnet, legacy-version and source-policy requirement on VTY lines 0–15.
steps: Edit the complete account document, inspect supplied login trials and verify every required outcome.
scenarios.explanation: Explicit default local-case login and local EXEC authorization select the local record check and its access level. Create only the two required records with their supplied training words; preserve their letter case and levels. Inspect both correct identities, wrong/case-varied inputs and the unchanged incoming policy. Training words are lesson data, not generated hashes.
hints: An incomplete method or record gets a document diagnostic. Creating one account alone does not complete the task.
The actual result names the matched account and level, or explains the failed comparison. A policy block is different from a wrong credential.
The valid word still matches, but the required level fails. Edits clear old checks; retry after repairing the document.
scenarios.simplifications: Checked2026-11-09: bounded CCNA200-301v1.1/5.3practice; Catalyst9300 IOS XE Dublin17.12 guides updated2023-07-28 and IOS AAA command reference. Explicit local-case login/local EXEC authorization only; case-sensitive named training records and levels1/15. Training words are saved lesson text, not real credentials or Cisco password hashes. No KDF, encoded secret, crypto, SSH session, host authentication, remote AAA/accounting, method fallback, non-AAA defaults, arbitrary command privileges or device conformance. Complete-document editing supports declared simple training words and preserves the existing virtual IPv4/incoming policy; it is not an incremental IOS session. Every check evaluates the source-held permitted account list and all incoming/login cases on each supplied line. Unsupported settings/failed paths cannot satisfy credential-rejection requirements. Practice has separate addresses, names, words and three supplied lines; assignment has sixteen. At most16records,8cases per category,64KiBdocument,2MiBsession. Trial observations are transient and never imported as execution evidence.

scenarios.title: Hand over privileged access without leaving an old account
scenarios.summary: Create the new maintainer, retain a restricted observer and retire the old account without weakening incoming access.
scenarios.objective: Hand over privileged access to NewMaintainer with training word Lab-Maintain-68 and privileged EXEC level 15. Keep Observer working with Lab-Observe-93 at user EXEC level 1. Remove FormerMaintainer from the complete account document; only NewMaintainer and Observer may remain. Rotating or renaming a surplus account does not retire it. Retain explicit local-case login and local EXEC authorization. Reject wrong training words, unknown names and the supplied differently cased name, while preserving all supplied incoming-access requirements on VTY lines 0–15.
steps: Edit the complete account document, inspect supplied login trials and verify every required outcome.
scenarios.explanation: Create the required maintainer at level15, retain Observer at level1 with its required word, and remove FormerMaintainer’s record. Changing a surplus record’s word or name still leaves an extra account. Keep local-case/local EXEC and the incoming-policy requirements. Correct credentials and correct access levels must both pass.
hints: Retirement concerns the record itself. Changing the old word or name is not equivalent to removing the extra account.
Both required identities should match with different levels. The former name should have no matching record after the handover.
Individual trial words may pass while an unexpected account remains. The account-list requirement catches that mistake alongside the incoming-policy checks.
